_note: Slots for [brg_our-restaurants-hero]. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Slot names are underscore-only. `text`/`textarea` defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`, which would double-escape and render as visible entity text.\n\nTHE <h1> IS WIRED. Approved editable by Sean 2026-08-13. LENGTH IS A HINT, NOT A LIMIT — under ~50 characters keeps it to 3 lines at 1440, but character count is only a proxy because WORD length drives the break: careers-hero renders 4 lines at 42 characters where community-hero renders 3 at 43, same rule and same width. 4 lines is the practical ceiling; at ~70 characters the headline is 5 lines and consumes the whole fold, pushing the next section off-screen. Measured, not guessed. The hero doodles were pinned to the padding band first (b324b35) so a longer headline can no longer drag one into the type — before that fix the top mark fell 43px between a 3-line and a 5-line headline and ended up level with the first line.

heading.default: Two brands. One standard. Zero compromises.

sub.label: Sub copy
sub.doc: Sits under the marker underline, capped at 52ch. Plain text; markup is escaped. PRESS RETURN to force a line break exactly where you want one.
sub.default: Every BRG location is built on the same foundation: quality ingredients, genuine hospitality, and a laid-back vibe worth coming back for.

uline_variant.label: Underline animation
uline_variant.doc: How the hand-drawn underline (line-restaurants-lg.svg) reveals. `u3` (default) filled brush + ~5deg angled wipe, keeps the taper. `wipe` straight-edged reveal, the conservative fallback. `u1` scaleX bar — this is what this hero used BEFORE the artwork swap, kept so the old look can be compared live. Unknown or blank renders the mark static and visible, never hidden. Catalog: website/lab/README.md.

bg_style.label: Background
bg_style.doc:
WHAT FILLS THE HERO BEHIND THE WORDS — one choice, and only that one's settings appear below. Until now a photo, a video, a pattern and the splash could all be set at once with nothing deciding between them, which is why it was hard to tell what you were looking at.

Photo is the full-bleed picture. Video plays a Vimeo or YouTube clip. Splash animation is the entrance from the coming-soon page. Pattern is a flat graphic wash. None leaves just the color.

Nothing is deleted when you switch — a photo you set is still there if you come back to Photo.

bg_photo.label: Background photo
bg_photo.doc: Optional. Leave this empty and the hero keeps the flat dark color it has today — nothing changes until you choose a photo. The photo fills the whole hero and is cropped to fit, so its exact size does not matter; around 1920px on the long edge is plenty and anything bigger only slows the page. Light photos make white headlines hard to read, which is what the two overlay settings below are for. If you also set a background video below, this photo is what shows while the video loads and for anyone who has animation switched off.

bg_photo_mobile.label: Background photo — phones
bg_photo_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the hero photo for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave empty and the main photo above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main photo is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or tighter version reads far better.

bg_photo_tone.label: Background photo — color
bg_photo_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

bg_photo_px.label: Background photo — movement
bg_photo_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

bg_photo_px_dir.label: Background photo — movement direction
bg_photo_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

video_id.label: Background video (optional)
video_id.doc: Paste a YouTube or Vimeo link, or just the ID. Leave blank to use the photo above, or the flat hero color if there is no photo. The video plays silently on a loop with no controls. The photo shows while the video loads, if the video is blocked, and for visitors who have switched off animation — so it is worth setting one as well.

video_source.label: Video from
video_source.doc: Which service the link is from. Only matters when a video is set.

splash_skater.label: Splash — full-screen photo
splash_skater.doc: The one that covers the whole hero and fades in while scaling down. Leave empty for the skater from the splash page.

splash_skater_on.label: Full-screen photo
splash_skater_on.doc: Hiding this leaves the three smaller plates on the dark base.

splash_tint.label: Side photos — veil
splash_tint.doc: A flat dark wash over the bottom-left and bottom-right photos only, so they sit back from the full-screen one behind them. It has always been 66% and had no control — set it to 0 to show those two photos at full strength. The soft fade at their edges is not affected; that is what stops them reading as rectangles.

splash_car.label: Splash — bottom left
splash_car.doc: Slides in from the left. Leave empty for the car from the splash page.

splash_surfer.label: Splash — bottom right
splash_surfer.doc: Slides in from the bottom right. Leave empty for the surfer from the splash page.

splash_crown.label: Splash — top right
splash_crown.doc: Fades in and sits small in the top corner. Leave empty for the spray crown from the splash page.

splash_crown_on.label: Top right
splash_crown_on.doc: This is the one plate that reads as a graphic rather than a photograph, so it has its own switch.

splash_skater_px.label: Splash — Full-screen photo — movement
splash_skater_px.doc: How far this plate drifts as you scroll, as a percentage of THAT PLATE's own height — so the same number moves the big background photo further than it moves the small corner mark, which is usually what you want. 0 is off. Set neighboring plates in opposite directions — that disagreement is what reads as depth. 40 is the ceiling.

splash_skater_px_dir.label: Splash — Full-screen photo — movement direction
splash_skater_px_dir.doc: Which way this plate travels as the page scrolls.

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below. ON A HERO THIS SITS BEHIND THE HERO PHOTO, so it only shows where that photo does not: with a background photo set, the photo covers the section edge to edge and this is hidden entirely. Use it on a hero with no photo, where it replaces the flat color.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

overlay_color.label: Overlay color
overlay_color.doc: A flat color laid over the background photo to keep the headline readable. This does nothing when no photo is set. Choose None to turn the overlay off entirely.

overlay_strength.label: Overlay strength
overlay_strength.doc: How much of the overlay color shows through. Only has an effect once an overlay color is chosen above. 45% is the usual setting for white type over a photo — go higher if the headline still fights the picture, lower if the photo is already dark.

mark_1_ast_circle_art.label: Artwork
mark_1_ast_circle_art.doc: Which mark is drawn here. Leave it alone to keep the one the design uses. Any SVG or PNG from the media library works; SVG stays crisp at any size.

mark_1_ast_circle_pos.label: Position
mark_1_ast_circle_pos.doc: Where the mark sits in its section. "Where the design put it" is the starting point and leaves it exactly where it is now — choose one of the nine only when you want to move it. Corners sit inside the section padding, so a long headline cannot push a mark down into the type.

mark_1_ast_circle_opacity.label: Opacity
mark_1_ast_circle_opacity.doc: How solid the mark is. 100 is as drawn; lower settles it into the background.

mark_1_ast_circle_show.label: Show this mark
mark_1_ast_circle_show.doc: Hiding removes just this one mark. Nothing else in the section changes.

mark_1_ast_circle_anim.label: Animation
mark_1_ast_circle_anim.doc: How the mark moves. "As built" keeps what it does today — a hard-cut jitter for most, a spin for the asterisk in the hero cluster. Still stops it entirely. Anyone who has switched off animation in their system settings sees it still whatever is chosen here.

cta_position.label: Where the buttons sit
cta_position.doc: At the bottom is the usual place and the one the rest of the site uses.

choices.foot: At the bottom of the section
choices.head: Directly under the heading

btn_size.label: Size
btn_size.doc: How big this section's buttons are. "As set site-wide" follows the Buttons tab on the Site-wide page; any single button can still differ on its own row.

btn_color.label: Button color
btn_color.doc:
The color for this section's buttons. "As designed" leaves them exactly as they are. Any one button can be given its own color in the list below — this is the one they fall back to.

Light, Dark, Accent and Alt accent are ROLES — what each one looks like is set once on the Site-wide page, so changing Accent there repaints every accent button on the site. The named shades below them are fixed colors for anything that has to be one particular color.

btn_hover.label: Button hover color
btn_hover.doc:
The color this section's buttons change TO when someone points at them. "As designed" means they keep their own color and the hover effect works it out — Fill in, for instance, swaps to the opposite ink so it always shows something.

This is what was missing: only the four ROLES had a hover color, set on the Site-wide page, so a button in one of the named shades had nothing to change to and effects that work by changing color did nothing at all.

btn_style.label: Filled or outline
btn_style.doc: Filled is a solid block of color. Outline draws the color as a ring with the words in it and nothing behind. Any one button can be set differently in the list below.

btn_effect.label: Hover effect
btn_effect.doc:
What the button does when someone points at it. Lift is what every button has always done and stays the default — it rises slightly and casts a shadow. Lift and swap color does that AND flips to the opposite ink, which is the loudest of the set and best kept for one main action on a page. Underline draws a rule under the words and leaves the button still, which reads as a link — a good fit for the small buttons. Grow swells it in place. Press down pushes it into the page. Fill in floods an outline button with its color, so pair it with Outline. None holds it still.

This is the HOVER only; the way the button arrives on screen is the site-wide reveal. Anyone who has switched off animation sees no hover movement whatever is chosen.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.doc:
Buttons for this section. Add as many as you need — they sit in a row and wrap onto the next line on a narrow screen. Leave the list empty, as it is now, and the section has no buttons at all and looks exactly as it does today.

Size, color, hover color, fill and hover effect are set for the whole section above; open any button's row and the same five controls are there for that one button. Left on "Same as the section" a button follows the section, and the section follows the Site-wide page.

label.label: Label
label.doc: The words on the button. Short reads best: it is set in capitals with wide letter spacing. A button with no label is not drawn.

href.label: Link
href.doc: Where it goes. A path like /careers/ stays on this site, a full address goes off it, and mailto:someone@blacktoprg.com opens a mail window.

popup.label: Open in a pop-up
popup.doc: For a Google Form, choose Pop-up and it opens in a panel over the page instead of sending people to Google. A form that is set to require a Google sign-in CANNOT be shown this way — Google's sign-in page refuses to be embedded and the panel comes up blank — so that one has to stay on Open the link until its Responses settings are changed. Anything that is not a form stays on Open the link.

color.label: Color
color.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's color above. Set it to make one button stand out from the others — a main button and a quieter second one, for instance.

hover.label: Hover color
hover.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's hover color above. Set it to give one button its own hover — a main button that flips to black while the quieter ones stay put.

style.label: Filled or outline
style.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow the section. The usual pair is a filled main button next to an outline one.

effect.label: Hover effect
effect.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" and this button follows the section's Hover effect, which in turn follows the site-wide one on the Site-wide page. Set it here to make one button behave differently from its neighbors.

size.label: Size
size.doc: Leave on "Same as the section" to follow it.

modal_bg.label: Pop-up background
modal_bg.doc: The color of the panel a form opens in. Match it to the form's own Theme color in Google Forms and the two read as one surface. This cannot color the form itself — that is Google's page on Google's domain.
